_comment: The dev-admin security contract: ONE answer key, four frameworks. Feature 127.
The /__dev dashboard can read files, run SQL, install packages and write routes,
so its whole security model rests on being dev-only AND safe on a dev machine that
also browses the web. This fixture pins the behaviour every framework must share
after the DEVADMIN-DEC-01/02/03/04/05/06 owner decisions - see
Every case is driven through the REAL dispatch pipeline (a real ASGI scope / a real
PSR request / a real Rack env / a real fetch against a bound server) - NO mocked
req/resp, because the audit found the prior Python+Node dev-admin tests mocked
req/resp and BYPASSED the gate. The witness is a real side effect: a file that is
NOT written, a DB row that is NOT inserted, a secret that is NOT returned. Python is
the REFERENCE implementation; the shapes asserted here are the canonical ones the
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework and a list of case names. The
four suites carry the SAME case names in each language's own idiom (Python
snake_case method, PHP testPascalCase method, Ruby it-description, Node assert
label), which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises and matches.

invariants.rule: With TINA4_DEBUG off the whole /__dev surface is ABSENT: a GET /__dev returns 404 AND a POST /__dev/api/file/save returns 404 and writes nothing. Proven behaviourally through the real server, not by inspecting a stage list or a route dict.
invariants.why: The gate is the one strong control and it was never behaviourally locked - only structural stage-list/route-dict inspection existed, and the primary Python+Node tests drove handlers through mock req/resp that bypassed the mount gate entirely. A behavioural prod-404 makes the dev-only contract a test, not a claim.
cases: dev admin is absent without debug

invariants.rule: With TINA4_DEBUG on, every /__dev mutation route (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) is fail-closed same-origin: a cross-site request (Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, or an Origin whose host differs from the request Host) is REFUSED and writes nothing; a same-origin request (Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin, or a matching Origin) is ALLOWED and performs the write. Closes drive-by CSRF/RCE from any page the developer visits.
invariants.why: The mutation routes had NO CSRF/Origin/Sec-Fetch/same-origin check in all four, and the body parsers accept no-preflight content-types (form-encoded/text-plain), so a cross-origin POST to /file/save then /reload was drive-by RCE on the dev machine. The framework CSRF middleware is post-match and never sees the pre-match /__dev stage, so the dashboard needs its own gate. Both cases together prove the gate DISCRIMINATES rather than blanket-denies.
cases: a cross origin write is refused and writes nothing
a same origin write is allowed

invariants.rule: The file endpoints NEVER serve secret material: GET /__dev/api/file?path=.env and GET /__dev/api/file/raw?path=.env are REFUSED (never return the .env contents / TINA4_SECRET), and the /__dev/api/files listing does NOT list .env. The denylist covers .env, .env.* (except the .env.example template), .git/, secrets/, and private-key material.
invariants.why: All four returned .env verbatim (Ruby+Node explicitly UN-hid .env in the listing), leaking TINA4_SECRET, the DB password, and TINA4_MCP_TOKEN/TINA4_API_KEY in cleartext - which nullifies the DB-URL redaction elsewhere and the leaked MCP token then unlocks REMOTE MCP. The witness is the secret string never appearing in any response body.
cases: the file read endpoint refuses dotenv secrets

invariants.rule: Defense-in-depth on top of the localhost-default bind: a /__dev mutation from a NON-loopback socket peer is REFUSED (reusing the MCP loopback check on the RAW socket peer, never X-Forwarded-For), while a loopback peer is ALLOWED. A spoofed X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 from a remote peer does NOT bypass it.
invariants.why: The default bind was 0.0.0.0 with no localhost restriction and no admin token, so a TINA4_DEBUG box on a shared network/container/WSL exposed the whole unauthenticated mutation+RCE+secret surface. The bind now defaults to 127.0.0.1 in dev; this invariant locks the request-level loopback refusal so a deliberately-exposed (TINA4_HOST) box still refuses remote mutations.
cases: a non loopback peer cannot mutate

invariants.rule: The injected dev toolbar HTML-escapes the reflected request path (and method): a request whose path contains <script> yields a toolbar in which the sequence appears escaped (<script>) and NEVER as a raw executable <script> tag.
invariants.why: Python and Node interpolated the raw request path into the toolbar HTML with no escaping, injected into every text/html response (including 404s), so a crafted path reflected <script> that runs in the dev-server origin and can then drive every ungated /__dev mutation route. PHP already escapes (htmlspecialchars); Ruby's toolbar is a static shell that never reflects the path - both keep a lock-in test so the property can never regress.
cases: the injected toolbar escapes the request path

invariants.rule: The injected dev toolbar carries NO inline style= attribute, NO onclick= (or any inline event handler) and NO inline <script> block - every script it emits is an external <script src=...> reference - so it renders under the framework's default default-src 'self' CSP with no violations. This is a mechanism-agnostic OUTCOME: PHP/Python/Node serve the CSS/JS as external /__dev/toolbar.{css,js} routes, Ruby's toolbar is a static inline-free shell, and all four must satisfy the same no-inline property.
invariants.why: tina4stack #115: under the strict default-src 'self' CSP the framework serves, an injected toolbar with inline style=/onclick=/<script> renders unstyled + non-functional and spews CSP violations (Node's toolbar alone had carried 22 inline style=, 4 onclick= and 5 inline <script> blocks). Python and Node moved the CSS/JS to external assets and wired every handler via addEventListener; PHP already served external /__dev/toolbar.{css,js}; Ruby's shell was already inline-free. This invariant locks the CSP-clean OUTCOME in all four so it can never regress, via a real-dispatch assertion on the ACTUAL injected toolbar bytes (no inline style=, no onclick=, no non-src <script>).
cases: injected toolbar has no inline style onclick or inline script

invariants.rule: The POST /__dev/api/mcp/call tool-invocation shim enforces the same two-layer MCP gate every other MCP surface enforces: a REMOTE UNAUTHENTICATED caller gets 404 BEFORE any tool runs (asserted by the real database_execute tool's write NOT landing in a real row), using the raw socket peer; a loopback caller runs the tool.
invariants.why: Python was the only framework whose /call shim was fail-open (its four siblings all gate); on a TINA4_DEBUG 0.0.0.0 box a remote unauthenticated caller could invoke database_execute/file_write. PHP/Ruby/Node already gate /call; this ports the gate to Python and locks all four with a real-dispatch, real-DB-write witness.
cases: a remote unauthenticated mcp call is refused and the tool does not run
